standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives that a quasi-finite impurity can be replaced by one over an elementary etale neighbourhood, and the second gives the corresponding statement starting from the henselization.

core_obligations: Record the trivial implication from an elementary etale neighbourhood to a quasi-finite morphism, and the two implications proved elsewhere (proof lines 4781-4786).

Prove the remaining implication: given an impurity over an elementary etale neighbourhood, factor the structure morphism from the henselization through it, choose a point of the henselization mapping to the given point and a point of the fibre over it mapping to the given impurity point, and observe that the resulting data form an impurity (proof lines 4787-4793).
Leave the technical verifications to the reader, as the author does (proof line 4794).
proof_roadmap: Factorization through the elementary etale neighbourhood and choice of points (proof lines 4787-4793).
Residual verifications left to the reader (proof line 4794).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects three equivalent formulations of the existence of an impurity, including one presented over the henselization of the base at the point (statement lines 4766-4779, tag 05J6-adjacent). Two implications are citations of earlier reductions, and the remaining one is proved by factoring the structure morphism from the henselization through the given elementary etale neighbourhood and choosing points of the henselization and of the fibre over them that inherit the impurity. The factorization argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
